methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Athanor operates in Robotics & Manufacturing, a sector populated by 1 public comparable (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. The company's stage and current valuation remain undisclosed, limiting precision in peer selection.

Peer-median valuation proved inapplicable. Despite identifying 11 same-sector peers in Robotics & Manufacturing, none satisfied narrow stage, adjacency, or valuation-tier filters required for robust multiples analysis. Zero same-stage, zero adjacent-stage, and zero similar-tier comparables were recoverable, falling short of the minimum three-datapoint threshold. Broadening to all-sector medians risked introducing systematic bias given heterogeneity in robotics subsegments, manufacturing verticals, and technology maturity.

The absence of triangulated analysis reflects a genuine data constraint rather than methodology failure. Without disclosed stage, funding history, revenue, or EBITDA for Athanor, and given the sparsity of truly comparable private robotics firms at equivalent development phases, conventional valuation approaches—peer multiples, DCF, or venture-method frameworks—cannot be reliably anchored to quantitative inputs. Forward progress on valuation requires either: disclosure of Athanor's stage and financial metrics, or identification of private peers with comparable funding rounds, technology scope, and market positioning. The public comparable may warrant independent analysis if sufficient financial data exists.
